title: Short: "Let go at the space station"

lines.text: Float a probe out of the space station, and let it go.
The station flies somewhere between three hundred and seventy and four hundred and sixty kilometres up.
Gravity up there is still about ninety percent of what it is on the ground. That's barely any weaker.
So you'd expect the probe to drop away, like anything you let go of down here.
It doesn't. It stays right beside the station, drifting along for lap after lap, as if nothing had happened.
lines.cue: caption: IT STAYS BESIDE THE STATION

lines.text: The station circles the Earth about every ninety minutes. That's sixteen laps of the planet every day.
lines.cue: caption: 90 MIN PER LAP / 16 A DAY

lines.text: And the probe does every one of those laps, side by side with the station.
Nothing is holding the probe up. Gravity is pulling it down, about ninety percent as hard as at the ground.
So why doesn't it fall? The full video on our channel has the answer. Like and subscribe so you don't miss the next one.
